items.title: Mitchel McAllister Interview, 1960-03-19
items.q: The interviewee does not mention Charlie McCurtis directly; the interviewer mentions him in the context of Walter Brundy taking lessons from him. The interviewee only confirms the name 'Walter Brundy' and corrects the interviewer's confusion with Douglas Williams.

ctx.x: Yes, he could play that. He was out of New Orleans. He was out of Baton Rouge. He came from Baton Rouge here with us. You remember when... You're going to remember. Douglas got killed on North Pine, Pine and Woodlawn. How long ago was that? Oh, it's been quite a bit. Just bubble up the colored boy that used to work for, uh, Williams and Williams. Now, he didn't get, you know, not fighting. He got killed by an automobile. Well, we used to have a store on the corner of Pine and Woodlawn. Well, right... We had it…
Coming out of Miss Lucille. Well, that's Charlie McCurtis. Got killed by the embalming drug here. I thought that was Charlie... Brundy. Yeah, Walter Brundy.
